evaluation_population: 1000 deterministically sampled labelled training rows (seed 42) from data/Train_data.csv (25,192 rows); risk scores are model-derived prioritization scores evaluated on the labelled training distribution

methodology.name: consensus_weighted_model_risk

components.anomaly_score: production model's P(anomaly) for the record (the same score predict.py exposes)
components.evidence_score: consensus_ratio = sum(shap) / sum(|shap|) over the record's full per-feature attribution list; directional agreement of the evidence in [-1, 1]

methodology.threshold_methodology: fixed policy thresholds anchored to the model's 0.5 operating point (predict.py's decision threshold): HIGH begins where a fully-consensual model-flagged record lands (s=0.5, consensus=1 -> 50); CRITICAL requires a flagged record with strong consensus (s=1.0, consensus>=0.6 -> 80); MEDIUM marks elevated but sub-threshold evidence. NOT fitted to data; quantile thresholds degenerate on the bimodal score distribution (75th percentile of the consensus-weighted score is ~95 on the sample below).
methodology.double_counting_analysis: SHAP explains the model output and P(anomaly) IS the model output (base + sum(shap) = P(anomaly)), so attribution magnitude is already inside the score: an additive-mass candidate was verified rank-identical to the score alone (Spearman 1.000 on a 1,000-row sample). The evidence therefore enters only through its directional consensus (multiplicative, bounded), which measurably reorders flagged records by evidence agreement (Spearman 0.879 vs the score-only order).
methodology.caveat: Risk scores are model-derived prioritization scores evaluated on the labelled training distribution. They are not probabilities of attack or compromise, not estimates of real-world impact, and not causal risk. The risk level prioritizes model alerts; it does not measure actual attack severity.

levels.definition: LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL prioritize model alerts; they are NOT claims about actual attack severity

excluded_unlabelled_dataset.reason_excluded: unlabelled (no ground-truth 'class' column); never evaluated, merged, or used to tune anything in this report
